content:
I create new project using lake +leanprover-community/mathlib4:lean-toolchain new crossword-lean math. That creates project, but it spawn lot of warnings due to missing header. That's fine for me, at the same time when I try to add header 

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Andrii Kurdiumov. All rights reserved.
Released under MIT license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Andrii Kuriumov
-/

The another issue of linter arise 

* 'Released under MIT license as described in the file LICENSE.':
Second copyright line should be "Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE."

Note: This linter can be disabled with `set_option linter.style.header false`

Trying to be smart, I add license = "MIT" to the lakefile.toml. And restart server. But that does not helps. What should I do now? I would like to not disable an linter, since that's great way to learning new tricks. Like have linter for example :slight_smile:
Setting the linter.style.header option in your lakefile to false disables only the header linter --- all other linters will continue to be active.
But I want header linter. Or Apache requirement it bolted into it ?
At the moment, the header linter hard-codes the Apache licence (since this is what mathlib uses) --- so the licence of your project is not taken into account at all.
Is this something for which I can submit PR?
If that doesn't make the code too hard to maintain, sure. You'd want to modify https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Tactic/Linter/Header.lean

Aah. So linter is part of Mathlib. Isn't it make sense to have linter (at least this kinf of linter) part of Lake or whatever more generic? I don't have appetite to make that happens, just asking out of curiousity.

Sure, it could make sense ---- but then the question starts what exactly the linter should enforce, how configurable it should be, etc. Right now, the linter enforces mathlib's convention. That's easy to specify :-)

That make sense in general, but maybe the new project with Mathlib creation should have this check disabled, no? Because for me as an outsider that sounds strange, and I think that issue on my part, and I go down rabbit hole or just learn to ignore warnings which is probbaly even worse
Right now I think the default is "switch everything on, and let downstream users switch off the ones they don't like".

@Andrii Kurdiumov Just to make sure you have the full picture, the way this works is that the template provided by lake +leanprover-community/mathlib4:lean-toolchain new <project_name> math places weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true in your lakefile, and linter.style.header is included within this. Some of the header linter's behavior is just being adjusted because it was only very recently discovered that its implementation meant it only worked within Mathlib. I do agree that it would be nice for the linters in this set, which are intended to be for standard usage downstream, to be as portable as possible, and you can maybe introduce a low burden option that takes the license name as an argument. Please note that you can also unset any individual linter within the set at your discretion.
